filings.business_description: NIKE sells NIKE Brand footwear and apparel. It sells through NIKE Direct, including NIKE Brand Digital and NIKE-owned stores, and through wholesale partners; the filing identifies consumers and wholesale partners in describing its marketplace. Its stated strategy includes product innovation, brand and sports marketing, and managing its direct and wholesale channels. A more detailed company description and a stated durable competitive edge are not available in the provided sources.
filings.risk_factors_summary: NIKE says its product, marketplace and brand-management actions have negatively affected, and may continue to negatively affect, revenue and profitability. In Greater China, declining store traffic, promotional activity and elevated inventory are hurting revenue and profitability; Converse is undergoing a strategic reset, with negative impacts from both expected throughout fiscal 2027. The company also describes uncertainty around U.S. and other countries’ import and export policies, tariff refunds and litigation. Competitive and technology-specific risk details are not available in the provided sources.
filings.mda_highlights: Fiscal 2026 revenue was $46.4 billion versus $46.3 billion in fiscal 2025, while currency-neutral revenue decreased 2%, primarily due to lower revenue in Greater China, Converse and EMEA. Footwear revenue was flat as lower average selling prices offset unit sales, while apparel revenue increased, supported by higher unit sales and average selling prices. Management said it expects to complete its product, marketplace and brand-management actions by the end of December 2026, and expects negative impacts from Greater China and Converse throughout fiscal 2027. The provided sources do not include Item 7, so additional MD&A discussion, including accounting changes, going-concern language or capital-raise announcements, is not available in the provided sources.
filings.key_regulatory_events: 10-K Item 1A: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that U.S. tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) on goods imported into the U.S. were unauthorized. The filing also reports tariff-recovery receivables and says NIKE will monitor related policy, refund and litigation developments.
